Re-fetched https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents and checked the new wording. The claim now uses the page's own 'specialized AI assistants that handle specific types of tasks' (plural), which removes the earlier one-type problem. The excerpt is on the page word for word but stops at 'file contents'; the page continues 'you won't reference again: the subagent does that work in its own context and returns only the summary'. The claim's second half is a little looser than the full sentence, but the same page says elsewhere that subagents help you 'Preserve context by keeping exploration and implementation out of your main conversation' and are for 'isolating operations that produce large amounts of output', so the claim is supported. Tidy-up: extend the excerpt and claim to include 'you won't reference again'. Vendor documentation, primary source. asOf stated.

Re-fetched https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices and checked the new wording. The hedge is now kept ('it isn't quite' matches the page's 'it wasn't quite'). The excerpt is on the page word for word, in the list under 'When a session doesn't go the way you expected, it's almost always one of these'. The claim attributes the statement to Anthropic's best practices page, which is correct (the page is titled 'Best practices for Claude Code'), and 'the usual cause' matches 'usually because'. This is vendor guidance with no data behind the causal claim; the attribution in the claim text handles that. Vendor documentation, primary source for how Anthropic advises using its own tool. asOf stated.

Judged only against the owner's words of 2026-11-27: 'Claude code evidence is weekendmvp.app itself all built solo, design, startup research over 200 ideas and many more features coming soon'. The record's ev-solo statement now contains that quote exactly (checked by string match). The owner said the site is the Claude Code evidence and that it was all built solo, so 'on his own with Claude Code' does not claim more. Notes: (1) the owner's message does not name himself; the record's 'John' is the link (the repo's Person schema is /john-iseghohi per CLAUDE.md), which I could not confirm from the quote alone. (2) This is an owner attestation, not a repo-verified fact; the visible git history shows one human author account (jeberulz) plus Claude, which is consistent but does not prove it. (3) Do not stretch it to say Claude Code was the only AI tool: CLAUDE.md also mentions a codex/wp44-audit-fixes branch.

Re-ran 'ls content/ideas/*.mdx | wc -l' in /home/user/weekendmvp on 2026-11-27: 231, which is more than 200 (earlier cross-check: ideas/manifest.json also has 231 entries and every MDX file has a manifest slug). The claim counts idea pages in the repository, which matches what the evidence counts. It says 'live in the repository', not 'published'; CLAUDE.md says new engine ideas stay on a private editorial path, so do not write 'published' or 'on the site' without checking. The count can drift.
